briefing.headline: OpenAI Orion and xAI Colossus push frontier capabilities as compute race intensifies

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race has accelerated with multiple frontier labs releasing advanced models this month. US-China tensions over chip exports remain high while safety concerns mount around production deployments.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI's Orion achieves new highs on agentic benchmarks while Anthropic's Claude 4.5 and Google's Gemini 3 compete closely. Meta open-sources Llama 4.1 and DeepSeek releases V3 with strong coding performance. xAI Colossus training run completes ahead of schedule.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New EU AI Act enforcement guidelines emphasize red-teaming requirements for high-risk systems.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA Blackwell ramp reaches 500k units monthly. Microsoft and Google announce major data center expansions in Texas and Arizona. TSMC reports record AI chip orders for Q4 2026.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI-level system emerge from a US lab or a Chinese state-backed effort by 2028?
